title: The Great Gatsby
synopsis: West Egg, 1922. A mansion next door throws parties without inviting anyone. The owner — Gatsby — has, you'll find, planned this evening for five years.

nodes.text: You rent next to Gatsby's mansion. The lawn glows.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Quiet.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Curious—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: East Egg, across the bay. Daisy, your cousin. Tom, her husband.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Family.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Tom takes you to the city. He keeps Myrtle.

nodes.text: You move home to the Midwest. You write the story down.

choices.consequence: “Begin to write” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Path.
You commit to “Burn the draft.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You write the book. It is, in the end, kind to Gatsby. The book outlives you. So do the parties, in their way.
You go home. You marry quietly. The Eggs become a long ago. You are, sometimes, in dreams, on the lawn again.
You stay in New York and become, against your better judgement, a bond salesman. You retire early. You buy a small green-lit dock somewhere upstate, just for the joke.
